notes: Identity checked independently from the supplied text: title What Counts as a Choice? U.S. Americans Are More Likely Than Indians to Construe Actions as Choices; authors Krishna Savani, Hazel Rose Markus, N.V.R. Naidu, Satishchandra Kumar, and Neha Berlia; DOI 10.1177/0956797609359908; Psychological Science 21(3), 391–398 (2010). This is the primary research article, with five studies, methods, results, figures, and references, rather than an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied. Only assigned original-side fields were examined; other fields are placeholders. No study number, description, outcome, or contrast is supplied. Page 4 (printed p. 394) contains Study 3 culture/condition/interaction tests and a cultural simple effect, as well as Study 4a logistic HLM results. Candidate printed metrics are d, F, t, beta, and odds ratio, rather than an identified Cohen's f^2 target. Study 3 reports 60 and 68 recruited students; Study 4a reports 39 and 84 recruited students. These are distinct study candidates, not eligible final analytic sums. No candidate is selected and no effect-size conversion is performed.
